run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T16:31:57Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is a downstream symptom of product-catalog being unavailable. The product-catalog Deployment (otel-demo, generation 4) was rolled to image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 at ~16:32; the new pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk cannot start (ImagePullBackOff, 401 UNAUTHORIZED resolving the manifest) and the only endpoint of the product-catalog Service is a not-ready address. frontend-proxy's ingress spans record HTTP 500 at a rate of ~4.8-7.3 spans/s from ~16:36 versus ~0-0.011/s before 16:32; those 500s are frontend responses whose own spans fail with gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE while dialing the product-catalog ClusterIP 100.69.9.250:8080. checkout and recommendation show their own error spans against the same product-catalog address. All other otel-demo deployments are 1/1 available and only product-catalog generated Warning events.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own spans are failing: the 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' operations carry status_tags error=true, http.status_code=500 and otel.status_code=ERROR in the incident window.

frontend-proxy ingress error rate (spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR) had a pre-incident baseline near zero (0 to 0.011 spans/s at the 16:10-16:32 evaluations) and jumped to 0.7375 at 16:34, then 4.84, 7.23, 7.32, 6.5, 7.30 and 5.21 spans/s at 16:36-16:46.

frontend spans show the failing dependency: operation 'grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' has error=true, rpc.grpc.status_code=14 with grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080 - Local (0.0.0.0:0)', and its parent route span 'executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId]' returns http.status_code=500.

The frontend GetProduct failure series appears only from the 16:36 evaluation onward (ERROR 3.37, 5.47, 5.61, 4.65, 5.60, 3.96 spans/s) while the corresponding UNSET series drops from ~9-10 spans/s (16:24-16:34) to 0 from 16:36, i.e. successful calls stopped and failures began after the product-catalog rollout.

The product-catalog Deployment (otel-demo, generation 4) runs image 'quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0' with imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent and reports condition Available=False, reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable, message 'Deployment does not have minimum availability.' (lastTransitionTime 2026-11-16T16:32:25Z); observedGeneration=4, updatedReplicas=1.

Pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk (owned by ReplicaSet product-catalog-56fbb5f966) is Pending with container product-catalog waiting in state ImagePullBackOff: 'Back-off pulling image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0": ErrImagePull: failed to pull and unpack image ...: 401 UNAUTHORIZED'; the pod is not Ready (ContainersNotReady) and has restartCount 0.

Events show the product-catalog rollout: old ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc scaled 1->0 and its pod killed/deleted at 16:32:17, and ReplicaSet product-catalog-56fbb5f966 scaled 0->1 at 16:32:25 creating product-catalog-56fbb5f966-8rw7j (then h9xjk), both new pods emitting Failed/ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff for the 401 image resolution.

The product-catalog Service has no ready endpoints: its Endpoints object contains only a notReadyAddresses entry (ip 100.96.4.116, targetRef pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk) on port tcp-service 8080, which matches the unreachable ClusterIP 100.69.9.250:8080 reported by callers.

recommendation is also affected through the same dependency: its 'get_product_list' and '/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts' spans fail with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and 'failed to connect to all addresses; last error: UNKNOWN: ipv4:100.69.9.250:8080: connect: Operation not permitted (1)'.

checkout is also affected through the same dependency: 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' fails with rpc.grpc.status_code=13 and 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product ...', and its child 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' span fails with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and 'dial tcp 100.69.9.250:8080: connect: operation not permitted'.

Checked and healthy: every other otel-demo Deployment reports available=1 and ready=1 (accounting, ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, postgresql, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart), while product-catalog alone shows available/ready <none> and unavailable 1; all non-product-catalog pods in the namespace are Running and Ready with 0 restarts.

The only Warning events in the otel-demo namespace during the window are the six product-catalog image-pull failures for product-catalog-56fbb5f966-8rw7j and product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk (Failed/ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff, 16:32:13-16:37:40Z); no other workload shows a Warning event.

frontend-proxy itself being misconfigured or failing internally is rejected: its error spans are the 'ingress'/'router frontend egress' hop of requests whose frontend spans carry http.status_code=500 caused by gRPC 14 to product-catalog, and the frontend-proxy pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts.

Scheduling or resource shortfall as the reason the product-catalog pod is Pending is rejected: the pod has PodScheduled=True and is assigned to node i-0c040f223cc7e47d7; its container never started and is blocked on ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff (401 UNAUTHORIZED).

The fault originates at the product-catalog Deployment's container image reference: it points at quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 (not the ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-* image used by the other services), and the registry answers 401 UNAUTHORIZED when resolving that manifest, so the image either does not exist or requires credentials this cluster does not provide. Which of 'wrong image name' versus 'missing registry auth' applies could not be determined because image pull secrets cannot be read.

The registry response is ambiguous between a deleted/renamed repository path and an auth problem: the message is exactly 'unexpected status from HEAD request to https://quay.io/v2/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid/manifests/1.0.0: 401 UNAUTHORIZED', which rules out a successful pull of that reference but does not by itself show whether the repository or the credentials are at fault.

gaps: The initial trace search for service frontend-proxy exceeded the result size limit (RESULT_TOO_LARGE, status error) and was only examined as a 60-row slice of 156 rows; spans beyond that slice are unknown, and the traces_search view itself is not citable.

kube-state-metrics series kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="otel-demo"} and kube_replicaset_owner{namespace="otel-demo",owner_name="product-catalog"} returned no data in this Prometheus (status no_data), so deployment availability and ReplicaSet ownership could only be read from live Kubernetes API state at query time (~16:47), not from a metric timeline.

The RequestErrorRate rule itself was not listed by the rules API (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data), so the exact alert expression and the annotation's 'current: 18.18888888888889' could not be reproduced or unit-checked; the error-rate rise is taken from traces_span_metrics_calls_total.

Container logs could not corroborate the traces: fetching logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-gx54w returned no lines for 16:25-16:47, and the pending product-catalog pod never started so it produced no application logs.

The alert start 2026-11-16T16:31:57Z precedes the first recorded rollout event (product-catalog old pod deleted 16:32:17Z) by about 20 seconds; the exact time of the first failing request is unknown and the first elevated 5-minute rate point is the 16:34 evaluation.
Image pull secrets and registry credentials cannot be read, so whether the 401 is caused by a wrong image path or by missing private-registry auth remains unresolved.

Trace data is a sampled view and the cited trace-derived views are flagged incomplete (more traces may exist); span counts, including the frontend-proxy error-span rate, are not unique request counts, so the user-facing error percentage is unknown.
next_steps: Inspect the product-catalog Deployment's last change (Helm release otel-demo, revision 2) to confirm why image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 was set, and restore the valid ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog image.
If the invalid image reference was intentional, verify imagePullSecrets and quay.io credentials for the it-bench repository before re-applying.
Confirm recovery by watching product-catalog reach Ready 1/1 and its Service gain a ready endpoint, then confirm frontend-proxy ingress 500 spans fall back to the pre-16:32 baseline.
Review whether the RequestErrorRate alert should separate upstream frontend 500s from proxy-originated failures, since the proxy was only relaying dependency-caused 500s.
